goals.goal: Moderators can review and tag an item in under 30 seconds.
goals.verdict: Median review-and-tag time is about 22 seconds on standard items, comfortably under the 30-second target; only long videos run over.
quotes: Median review-and-tag time is around 22 seconds on standard items, down from roughly 45 in the old tool.
Video preview loads fast and the tag panel is right next to it. Much quicker than before.
Moderator cleared short-form clips in 15–25 seconds each; longer videos took closer to a minute, which the team considers expected.

goals.goal: Escalated sensitive content reaches the risk & response team within 5 minutes.
goals.verdict: Escalations routinely take 12–40 minutes to reach R&R because there is no alerting, acknowledgment, or severity ordering — far outside the 5-minute target.
quotes: Escalated a self-harm livestream at 2:14pm and R&R didn't pick it up until 2:41. That's 27 minutes on something that should take 5.
Watched a moderator escalate a child-safety item, then wait about 12 minutes before messaging the R&R on-call directly because the tool showed no acknowledgment.
Team leads report escalations sit in a shared inbox with no alerting — R&R only sees them when someone refreshes the page.

goals.goal: Moderators only see queues they're authorized for.
goals.verdict: No access incidents since launch; moderators and leads say queue scoping works as intended, including for new hires.
quotes: Love that I only see the queues I'm trained for now. Way less noise.
New hire onboarding was smooth. She only saw the Spam queue until she finished graphic content training. Exactly what we wanted.
No access incidents reported since launch. Permission requests route through leads and take about a day, which everyone is fine with.

goals.goal: Policy tags are clear and consistent across moderators.
goals.verdict: Hover descriptions help, but moderators disagree on overlapping tags (about 12% disagreement in QA) and the tag list is hard to scan.
quotes: Is 'graphic violence' vs 'violent extremism' about intent or content? Three of us tagged the same video three different ways today.
QA found about 12% disagreement between the 'harassment' and 'bullying' tags in last week's audit sample.
Policy tag list is too long. I scroll past 30 tags to find 'spam'.

goals.goal: Team leads can see queue volume in real time to plan staffing.
goals.verdict: Leads value the dashboard, but a 15–20 minute lag and no per-queue or per-hour view mean it isn't real-time enough to staff thin queues.
quotes: Team leads say the volume dashboard lags 15–20 minutes behind the actual queue, so staffing calls get made on stale numbers.
We only have about 3 trained moderators per queue. When one calls out, I can't see the backlog building until it's already 200+ deep.
Team lead kept the old staffing spreadsheet open next to the dashboard to cross-check numbers during morning standup.

unplanned.title: Tool slows or fails during livestream spikes
unplanned.summary: When live-event traffic spikes, the queue view slows to 10+ seconds per item, freezes, or throws errors that force a refresh and lose the moderator's place.
quotes: Tool froze for about 2 minutes during the Saturday night livestream spike. Couldn't load any videos.
During big live events the queue view takes 10+ seconds to load each item, and moderators fall behind fast.
Getting 'Something went wrong' every time traffic jumps. I have to refresh and I lose my place in the queue.

unplanned.title: No keyboard shortcuts
unplanned.summary: Every action requires the mouse. Moderators report wrist strain over long shifts and miss the J/K navigation and number-key tagging from the old tool.
quotes: Please add keyboard shortcuts. Clicking for every tag and every 'next' is killing my wrist by hour six.
Every moderator observed reached for the mouse for every action: approve, tag, next. Two were wearing wrist braces.
The old tool had J/K to move between items and number keys for tags. We lost all of that in v1.

fixNext.title: Escalations take 12–40 minutes to reach Risk & Response

stoppage.rationale: Moderators stall on escalated items and fall back to Slack to chase R&R manually.

impact.rationale: Affects every moderator who escalates and the whole R&R team; 7 reports across all four channels.

urgency.rationale: Self-harm and child-safety content waiting 12–40 minutes is a direct safety and compliance exposure.

fixNext.title: Tool slows or fails during livestream spikes

stoppage.rationale: The tool freezes or errors out entirely, so moderators cannot review anything.

impact.rationale: Hits all moderators on shift, but only during live-event spikes.

urgency.rationale: Spikes coincide with the highest volume of harmful live content.

fixNext.title: Queue volume isn't visible in real time for staffing

stoppage.rationale: With about 3 trained moderators per queue, one absence can quietly create a 200+ item backlog.

impact.rationale: Every team lead is affected, and understaffed queues slow down all moderators on them.

urgency.rationale: Staffing decisions are made daily on data that's 15–20 minutes stale.

stoppage.rationale: Work continues, just slower and with more physical strain.

impact.rationale: Every moderator, every item, every shift; some already wear wrist braces.

urgency.rationale: Ergonomic risk builds over time rather than causing an immediate incident.

fixNext.title: Overlapping policy tags cause inconsistent decisions

stoppage.rationale: Moderators can still tag items; the problem is consistency, not blockage.

impact.rationale: About 12% disagreement on common tags skews enforcement and QA metrics.

urgency.rationale: Inconsistent enforcement creates audit and policy-compliance risk.
